title: Gunman was former employee
article: Jean Claude Hubert had just fired up the barbecue Wednesday night when his longtime neighbour, Rainer Elsner, 65, came running into his backyard, bleeding from the head and yelling "I've been shot. I've been shot."
Hubert, 68, shouted for his wife to call 911 around 5:45 p.m. and quickly got a blanket for Elsner, now turning white and shaking.
Moments earlier, on normally quiet Bear Hill Road in Ottawa's rural west side, a lone suspect had broken into Elsner's home and shot him at least three times -- in the back, arm and head.
Elsner told his neighbour and police that the gunman was a former employee he had accused of forging cheques.
Elsner also told police the shots sounded more like pops, rather than bangs, leading a responding police officer to suggest the suspect may have been armed with a pellet gun.
Elsner was able to give police enough information for an all-points bulletin, leading to a high-speed pursuit that ended with officers shooting the suspect in the chest on the side of Highway 417.
Police broadcast a description of the suspect and his car, and at about 6 p.m., a patrol car saw a vehicle matching the description heading east along Highway 417 near Parkdale Avenue.
Police tried to stop the car, and ended up chasing the vehicle before it was stopped in the eastbound lanes of the highway near Walkley Road.
There, a man -- identified by a family member as Richard Bastien -- was shot by police. He was unconscious and underwent extensive surgery on Wednesday.
On Thursday afternoon, he was in critical condition and was on life support, said Ontario's Special Investigations Unit spokesman Frank Phillips.
Joanne Bastien, who identified herself as Richard Bastien's sister-in-law, said his family is very upset and had heard little from police.
"They're quite frustrated and confused."
Richard Bastien is the youngest of 11 siblings, she said. He and his common-law wife had lived in Gatineau, but moved about six months ago, Bastien said.
After the shooting, a section of Highway 417's eastbound lanes near Walkley Road was closed until Thursday morning, while the incident was investigated.
The SIU has identified one subject officer -- an officer who would have been directly involved in what happened -- and four witness officers in the incident.

Seven SIU investigators, including four field and three forensic, are in Ottawa. The investigation centres on the incident that took place on the 417 at Walkley Road, beginning with the car being stopped, Phillips said.
Ottawa police major crime investigators are probing the shooting on Bear Hill Road. Initial reports had indicated the call to police had involved a robbery.
Hubert said while his neighbour waited for an ambulance, he said the gunman was a former employee who had stolen and forged some of his cheques.
Elsner, a widower, often spent his free time birding, and has written to the Citizen about sightings in the past.
"He is such a good neighbour. He didn't even want to come in because he didn't want to get blood on our floors," Hubert said Thursday.
"He was bleeding from the head, elbow and back," said Hubert, pointing to bloodstains on his deck.
Ottawa police said Elsner was in stable condition in hospital Thursday.
An eyewitness told the Citizen the police shooting happened around 6:15 p.m. Joel Lehoux said he was passed at high speed by a car with Quebec licence plates on the 417, just past Walkley.
The car was followed by Ottawa police cruisers, Lehoux said. He said the car stopped or was pulled over on the shoulder of the highway about a kilometre past Walkley Road.
"I saw police take cover, aiming their guns at the car. I didn't hear any shooting, but I thought I saw a body in the field about 10 metres from the car," he said.
Soon around two dozen cruisers had swarmed the area.

The SIU was notified of the case at 6:39 p.m. Three officers "interacted" with a man who got out of the car and during the "interaction," an officer fired at least one shot, hitting the man, the SIU said in a statement.
It was the second Ottawa police shooting involving a person in a little over a month, and third in the past four months.
In a case that remains under SIU investigation, suspected bank robber Paul Michael Jeffrey, 27, was shot dead in Ottawa's east end last month.
On Dec. 29 of last year, an Ottawa officer shot and injured two people with one bullet when confronted by a knife-wielding woman in a Pinecrest Road apartment.

The bullet passed through the woman and hit a man in another room at the apartment. The SIU cleared the officer of any criminal wrongdoing, saying the woman took an aggressive stance with the weapon and ignored orders to drop it, moving towards the officer.

Steve Boucher, president of the Ottawa Police Association, said the association is making sure officers, communications centre workers and other staff who dealt with the Wednesday evening incidents "have their support groups in place to get them through this.
"When our members go through these events, it's very stressful on them," Boucher said.
